title: Gaps Between the Smallest and Largest
statement:
You get an array nums of distinct integers in any order. Once it held every integer from its smallest value to its largest value, but some values in between were lost. The smallest and largest values are still there.

Return every missing integer strictly between the smallest and largest value, in increasing order. Return an empty list if nothing is missing.

examples.why: The range is 3 to 7. Only 4 and 6 are absent.
9, 10 and 11 are all present, just not sorted.
The range comes from the values, not from the first and last element of the array.

hints: First find the smallest and largest value. They define which numbers should exist.
For every number in that range you need to know: is it in nums? Make that check O(1).
Put nums in a set (or a boolean array indexed by value), then walk from min + 1 to max − 1 and collect what is absent. Walking in order gives a sorted result for free.

explain.intuition:
The values that should exist are exactly min, min + 1, …, max. So the job is: for each number in that range, is it present? Checking with includes costs O(n) per number. A set, or a boolean array indexed by value since values are at most 100 000, answers each check in O(1).

Walking the range upward also produces the answer already sorted. No sort needed, which is the second thing people get wrong.
steps: Put every value in a set.
For v from lo + 1 to hi − 1, push v to the answer if the set does not contain it.
pitfalls: Taking the range from nums[0] and nums[n−1]. The array is not sorted.
Including lo or hi themselves; they are always present.
Calling includes inside the range loop, which is O(range · n).

solutions.title: Search for each value
solutions.idea: Walk the range and scan the array for each value.

solutions.title: Sort and fill the gaps
solutions.idea: Sorted, every jump bigger than 1 between neighbours hides the values in between.

solutions.title: Set and range walk
solutions.idea: Store the values, walk from min to max, keep what is absent.

followups: Values can be as large as 10<sup>18</sup> but only a few are missing. Which version still works, and why does the set walk not?
Return the missing values as compact ranges like "4-6" instead of single numbers.
